output.brief:
The Android login drop is most likely caused by the 3 March edge-protection rule update from Corvane, not by Android release 6.14 or by attackers. Rule AUTO-LIB-17 began blocking password logins from the Android app at 10:41 UTC on 3 March, the same minute the failures started. About 41,300 real, previously successful installs were blocked, and the same failures appear on every app version, including 6.11 and older, and on every OS version. iOS and quick-unlock were not affected. I am fairly confident in this. The main remaining gap is that I did not check the auth-service data or the vendor's written explanation.

Next steps: ask Corvane to set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the mobile password path while keeping rate limits and lockout active, then confirm that Android password success recovers. Do not raise bot sensitivity or remove attempts from the KPI, since both would hide or worsen the problem. Do not roll back 6.14 on this evidence. Treat the contact-centre rise as a separate question, since the fee mailing also explains it.
output.methodChoice: EDF diagnostic sequence; collected X1 and X14 (2 of 2 items).
